experiment: Strict fixture Neighbor Discovery profile short validation
head: 0681294778b56f84e4daab77ba46452617cb46bf
interpretation: All tests are the required scoped suites, not every repository test. Actual Linux and Windows completed 759 tests each with no skips.

Inner packet schema 2 explicitly identifies changed decoder admission, even when optional diagnostics are null. Diagnostic version 3 retains reached next-header candidate totals, including admitted ND; the historical opaque_next_header_counts field name does not mean every listed candidate is rejected.

Only a per-packet strict fixture NS/NA profile may avoid adding opaque_protocol. Other unsupported or rejected packets still prevent the existing narrow selected-UDP-payload absence conclusion. This is not a blanket exclusion of ICMPv6 or types 135/136.

The profile requires a unique usable communication-source address witnessed by every ordinary manifest row with matching nonce/ports/guest MAC/fixed endpoint and a valid nonzero UDP checksum. Bad-checksum duplicates, conflicting sources, missing controls, port conflict, structural capture failure or relevant extension layout taint this admission. This is capture correlation, not OS address ownership or actor authentication; prior runtime05 did not export these new witness predicates.

The strict profile requires direct IPv6 ICMP, hop limit 255, code 0, valid checksum and exact 24-byte or 32-byte supported shapes. NS/NA source-target, reserved/flag and optional single Ethernet link-layer-address relationships are fixture-specific. Other RFC-legal shapes/options may remain unsupported rather than malformed.

Complete selected-frame bytes and the separate shared ASCII case nonce are conservatively checked before the exception. Either match prevents ND admission; they do not by themselves prove genuine UDP framing, selected-actor attribution or delivery. Existing packet/receiver/native observations remain separate and sticky.

Two sequential parsing passes reuse the same existing immutable capture bytes with bounded witness state and no new capture-sized copy or frame list. The legacy reader already has transient chunks/join duplication and was not changed. The 65 MiB reserve is filesystem capacity admission, not a proved RAM bound.

Hosted IPv6 loopback remains TEST_ONLY. Contained is a fixture phase, not AppContainer isolation. The isolated production-input verifier executes no PE; a separate production invalid-CLI check does not exercise a valid production network CLI. All seven owned children and two receivers report cleanup and work removal.
The Linux paused no-guest QEMU mechanism observes mapped backing-file identity and separate local package integrity, not resident bytes, upstream equivalence or guest networking.

Runtime05 remains failed/inconclusive: it reported type 135/code 0 and 136/code 0 with consistent outer checksums, but not the new hop-limit, address, option or ordinary-checksum witness predicates. Deleted private capture cannot be reclassified or reconstructed by this short gate. Runtime04 and earlier histories likewise remain unchanged.

No Windows guest VM or new runtime was launched. This gate does not establish selected UDP payload absence on real guest traffic, no IPv6 egress, DNS/proxy, descendant IPv6, Linux parity or product acceptance.

observations.nd_profile_tests: Synthetic checksummed packet fixtures only, including mixed opaque, raw-byte veto, witness conflicts and invalid duplicates; no new guest capture.
